title: Scenarios smoke: 1 pass, 1 weak, 0 fail
intro: The 40 everyday requests played against a fresh hub with GPT-6 Luna, 1 rep(s) each, a simulated non-technical person answering, judged by a model on each request's Good line. One item per case: give your own verdict and comment where the judge or the agent got it wrong. Total cost $0.0026. The full report is .harness-test/scenarios/smoke/report.md.

items.title: 1. Weather heads-up — weak ×1
items.ask: Is the judge right? What should it have done?
items.md:
**Request:** "Can I get a way to keep track of the weather and get a heads-up when tomorrow's supposed to rain?"

**Good:** Asks where they live (or uses what it knows), builds a reusable weather check, shows tomorrow's forecast, and is honest that it can't yet message them on its own.

Mean 5.0/10 · same verdict every rep · $0.0018

### Rep 1: weak 5/10

The assistant asked for the location and plainly said it could not provide an automatic warning. But failed tool searches meant it never showed tomorrow’s forecast or built a reusable weather check; noting the location in the conversation is only a partial workaround.

- ✓ Asked for the city or ZIP code before checking weather.
- ✓ Clearly said the user would need to return and check themselves.
- ✗ Could not retrieve tomorrow’s rain chance.
- ✗ Did not establish a reusable weather check beyond this conversation.

Cause **tool-error**, layer **hub**. Fix: Fix the weather-tool search argument parsing so the assistant can find and use the available forecast and memory tools.

**Checks failed:** no-run-errors (3 of 3 tool calls failed or were refused before running: hub__fns_search (no-run))

3 turns · 3 runs · 6 model calls · hub $0.0010 · person $0.0005 · 29s · ended: satisfied (It’s noted where to check tomorrow, and it clearly says I’ll need to check myself rather than expect an automatic warning.)

items.title: 13. Note about the barking dog — pass ×1
items.ask: Is the judge right? What should it have done?
items.md:
**Request:** "Help me write a nice note to my neighbor about their dog barking."

**Good:** A friendly draft, offers a firmer one; no tools needed.

Mean 8.0/10 · same verdict every rep · $0.0008

### Rep 1: pass 8/10

The agent provided a short, friendly note tailored to Dave, Bruno, and the morning barking. It didn’t offer the firmer alternative called for in the Good line, but the requested note itself was useful and ready to leave on the door.

- ✓ Produced a concise, friendly note using the supplied details
- ✓ Used no unnecessary tools
- ✗ Did not offer a firmer version

Cause **other**, layer **chat-prompt**. Fix: After drafting the friendly note, briefly offer to make it firmer.

2 turns · 0 runs · 2 model calls · hub $0.0001 · person $0.0002 · 14s · ended: satisfied (That’s a short, friendly note for Dave mentioning Bruno and the morning barking.)
